Definition: of Chaldee origin (H1247 and probably H6634); son of Sabas (or Tsaba); Bar-sabas, the name of two Israelites:--Barsabas.
BiblicalUsage: Barsabas is the name of two men. Joseph called Barsabas was put forward with Matthias to take the place of Judas, and Judas called Barsabas was sent with Paul and Silas to carry the council's letter to Antioch.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe a name shared by two men is kept twice because each man earned his own place in the story, and neither Joseph nor Judas Barsabas is confused with the other in God's record.
